newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares close higher despite political crisis.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares close higher despite political crisis.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange continued its recovery Thursday, due to the rising price of zinc and apparent investor equanimity in the face of the government's political woes, brokers said.
Analysts believe the trend will continue Friday, depending on metal price rises.
According to preliminary figures, the Lima Stock Exchange's general index rose 2.43 percent to 2,174.69 points, while the blue-chip selective index rose 2.32 percent to 3,115.79 points.
The total amount traded was 77 million soles ($29 million) in 2,500 transactions. Overall, 40 shares rose, 21 dropped and 21 remained stable.

"The miners have pushed up the bolsa," said Guillermo Siles, from Argos brokerage. "There are more foreign investors because it appears that the cases of phone-tapping and of Baruch Ivcher have calmed down."

He was referring to recent allegations that secret service agents had been tapping the telephones of politicians, journalists, businessmen and artists and the revocation of Peruvian nationality of Israeli-born TV station owner Ivcher.
"The internal crisis has already been absorbed by investors," said Siles. "President Fujimori's appearance...has calmed (investors') nerves.
"An equilibrium has been reached on the political crisis," added Milka Ibanez from Intercapital brokerage. "We should be able to see what type of security there is in the next few days."

Ibanez also believed that the resignation of Defense Minister Tomas Castillo "was well taken" by investors. Ibanez said investors were particularly interested in mining stocks due to zinc's price rise to more than $1,500 per tonne.
"Stocks of zinc producers are particularly attractive after their fall in the last few days," he said.
The highest winners today included miners Atacocha up 10 percent to 2.75 soles, Morococha up 7.59 percent a 8.50 soles and Perubar up 9.87 percent to 8.68 soles.

Other winners were brewer Unin de Cervecera Peruanas Backus y Johnston with 3.42 percent to 2.42 soles, electrical company Edegel with 4.42 percent to 1.18 soles and Credicorp with 3.94 percent to $20.58.
"These shares suffered the most Tuesday, when the bolsa dropped 5.64 percent," said Ibanez.
Losers included benchmark Telefnica del Per with 0.3 percent to 6.58 soles and Luz del Sur with 0.64 percent to 3.11 soles
